newsitem.title: UK: Palladium rallies on Russia delays.
newsitem.headline: Palladium rallies on Russia delays.

text.p: The price of palladium rallied on Monday on a prospect of new delays to Russian exports of the rare white metals to Japan, and this also helped gold to edge higher.

Palladium, used mainly in the automotive sector, gained $5.25 to $152.00/$153.00 per ounce. Dealers cited comments by the Russian trade representative to Japan that there would be no shipments in April and those in May were in doubt.
"The response to that was that there was quite a bit of borrowing around. Clearly people are yet again taking note of that," said one dealer.
He was "flabbergasted" by the market's reaction to the remarks as it had been aware of delays since Russian sales contracts expired in January and problems arose over renegotiating them.
But "if people are short and if it starts to move up they get concerned about it."

The rise in palladium helped platinum gain ground as it stood $2.50 higher at $365.00/$366.00. The Russian contracts involve all platium group metals (PGM), but palladium is centre stage as Russia is the world's biggest supplier.
Gold and silver edged up with a dose of short covering after a shift in sentiment as prices continued to recoup last week's losses. But dealers were cautious about upside prospects.
"We've got a bit of upside potential still but I'm not getting overexcited just at the moment," said one dealer.
"If we can get a little bit of a rally going then we might encourage some large short covering in silver," he added.
Bullion fixed higher at $349.00 an ounce versus $347.85, but the cash market struggled to stay above $349.00 to pave the way for a move towards $350.00 and the $352.00 resistance.
It was indicated at $348.45/$348.95 in late dealings from Friday's $347.40/$347.70.
Support held well at $347.00 earlier, but dealers said it could still falter unless the market gathered upside momentum.

Silver continued to emerge from last week lows with New York correcting after a wave of fund selling, but it too failed to keep up the momentum, failing to clear initial resistance at $4.80. Comex May futures were up 4.30 cents at 478.50.

Analysts said a break above $4.80 might prompt short covering towards $4.90 and even $5.00. But as things stood, prices remained prone to continued downside risk with critical support pegged at $4.55/$4.60.
Silver was indicated at $4.79/$4.81 an ounce at 1535 GMT after a brief surge to $4.80 earlier and against Friday's $4.72/$4.74. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 7729
